stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> iff <math><mi>𝐺</mi></math> is a disjoint union of cliques.</em></div><div><em>Proof of <a href="#thm-zero-var">Theorem 4</a>.</em> If <math><mi>𝐺</mi></math> is a disjoint union of cliques then, since every labeling of a clique has a unique local maximum, each clique contributes exactly one peak under <em>any</em> labeling, so <math><mi>𝑆</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝜅</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐺</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math><mi>𝑇</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜅</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐺</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> are constant (isolated vertices are cliques of size <math><mn>1</mn></math>, each its own component). Conversely, a graph is a disjoint union of cliques iff it contains no induced path on three vertices. So if <math><mi>𝐺</mi></math> is not such a union it has vertices <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi></math> with <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐸</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>∉</mo><mi>𝐸</mi></math>. Fix any assignment of the <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math> smallest labels to <math><mi>𝑉</mi><mo lspace="0.2222222222222222em" rspace="0.2222222222222222em">\</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math>, and give <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi></math> the three largest labels. The peak status of every vertex outside <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math> is then identical in all such labelings: such a vertex ranks below <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi></math>, hence is a non-peak if adjacent to any of them and otherwise sees only the fixed outside labels. Among <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math>, <math><mi>𝑎</mi></math> is a peak iff <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>𝑏</mi></math> (its only possibly-larger neighbor), likewise <math><mi>𝑐</mi></math> iff <math><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>𝑏</mi></math>, and <math><mi>𝑏</mi></math> iff it exceeds both <math><mi>𝑎</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑐</mi></math>. Ranking <math><mi>𝑏</mi></math> below both <math><mi>𝑎</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑐</mi></math> gives <math><mn>2</mn></math> peaks, and ranking <math><mi>𝑏</mi></math> above both gives <math><mn>1</mn></math>. The two labelings are equally likely and give peak counts differing by <math><mn>1</mn></math>, so <math><mi>𝑆</mi></math> is non-constant and <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><div><strong>Proposition 4 (restated).</strong> <em>On the monochrome star, <math><mtext>ℙ</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑗</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math> for <math><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math> and <math><mtext>ℙ</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math>, with the mean and variance of <a href="#eq-star">Eq. (7)</a>.</em></div><div><em>Proof of <a href="#prop-star">Proposition 4</a>.</em> By <a href="#lem-reduction">Lemma 1</a>, <math><mi>𝑇</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑆</mi></math>. On the star a leaf is a peak iff its label exceeds the center’s (its only neighbor), and the center is a peak iff it holds the maximum label. Let <math><mi>𝑐</mi></math> be the label rank of the center. For <math><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>𝑛</mi></math> the <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑐</mi></math> leaves above the center are the peaks, so <math><mi>𝑇</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑐</mi></math>. For <math><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi></math> the center is the unique peak and <math><mi>𝑇</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. As <math><mi>𝑐</mi></math> is uniform on <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math>, the value <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> arises from both <math><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi></math>, giving the stated law. The moments and their expansion are a direct computation. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><div><strong>Lemma 2 (restated).</strong> <em>For distinct vertices <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></math> with peak indicators <math><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub></math>, <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Cov</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn></math>, with the finer classification stated in the body.</em></div><div><p><em>Proof of <a href="#lem-cov-bound">Lemma 2</a>.</em> Adjacent vertices are never both peaks, so there <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Cov</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix">−</mo><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. For non-adjacent <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></math> with parameters <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> (<math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑏</mi></math>, <math><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑏</mi></math>), draw i.i.d. uniform <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> values (equivalent to a random labeling) and condition on the values <math><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑡</mi></math> of <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></math>: a private neighbor of <math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> must fall below <math><mi>𝑠</mi></math>, one of <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> below <math><mi>𝑡</mi></math>, and a common neighbor below <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">min</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, so</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msubsup><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msup><mi>𝑠</mi><mi>𝑎</mi></msup><msup><mi>𝑡</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msup><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">min</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑏</mi></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(28)</div></div>the square being split along its diagonal: on <math><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>𝑠</mi></math> the inner integral is <math><msup><mi>𝑠</mi><mrow><mi>𝑎</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, on <math><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>𝑡</mi></math> it is <math><msup><mi>𝑡</mi><mrow><mi>𝑎</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Subtracting <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> over the common denominator gives <a href="#eq-cov-closed">Eq. (8)</a>, the numerator being <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑏</mi></math>. The rest is read off <a href="#eq-cov-closed">Eq. (8)</a>. The covariance vanishes with <math><mi>𝑏</mi></math>. For <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math> the three factors of the denominator are at least <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, with equality iff <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, whence the bound <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, which is <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn></math> at <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>18</mn></math> at <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and decreases afterwards (there <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></math>). For <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> one of the first two factors is at least <math><mn>3</mn></math> and the third at least <math><mn>4</mn></math>, whence <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>24</mn></math>. For <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> the denominator is <math><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Equality in <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Cov</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn></math> thus requires <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>: two leaves with the same single neighbor. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><div><strong>Theorem 6 (restated).</strong> <em>For every <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, among all graphs on <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> vertices, <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is maximized by the star <math><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> and by no other graph.</em></div><div><p><em>Proof of <a href="#thm-star-exact">Theorem 6</a>.</em> We first prove the statement among graphs without isolated vertices, for every <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. For <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> the only such graph is the edge <math><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, and for <math><mn>3</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></math> the statement was checked by exhaustive enumeration of all labeled graphs without isolated vertices (<a href="#sec-app-numerics">Appendix G</a>). Let <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>7</mn></math> and let <math><mi>𝐺</mi></math> be a graph on <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> vertices without isolated vertices, other than <math><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math>. Call a vertex of degree <math><mn>1</mn></math> a <em>leaf</em> and its unique neighbor its <em>hub</em>. Write <math><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub></math> for the number of leaves at <math><mi>𝑤</mi></math>, <math><mi>𝐿</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub></math> for the number of leaves, <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐿</mi></math> for the number of vertices of degree at least <math><mn>2</mn></math>, and <math><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">max</mo><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>𝐿</mi></math>. The star is the graph with <math><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. If <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> then <math><mi>𝐺</mi></math> is a perfect matching and <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> by <a href="#thm-zero-var">Theorem 4</a>, so let <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. We bound <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑢</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≠</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></mrow></msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Cov</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> class by class with <a href="#lem-cov-bound">Lemma 2</a>, writing <math><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> for <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</p><p><em>Diagonal.</em> <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑋</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>4</mn></math> for a leaf and at most <math><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>9</mn></math> for a vertex of degree at least <math><mn>2</mn></math>: at most <math><mi>𝐿</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>9</mn></math> in all.</p><p><em>Two leaves.</em> Two leaves at the same hub have parameters <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and covariance <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn></math>. Two leaves at distinct hubs have no common neighbor and covariance <math><mn>0</mn></math>, unless they form an isolated edge, with negative covariance. The ordered pairs of leaves at a common hub number <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>𝐿</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</p><p><em>A leaf and a vertex of degree at least 2.</em> Let <math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> be a leaf at <math><mi>𝑤</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>𝑤</mi></math> a vertex of degree at least <math><mn>2</mn></math>. The pair is non-adjacent, and has a common neighbor iff <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> is adjacent to <math><mi>𝑤</mi></math>. Its parameters are then <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and its covariance <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>24</mn></math>. Every neighbor of <math><mi>𝑤</mi></math> that is not a leaf at <math><mi>𝑤</mi></math> has degree at least <math><mn>2</mn></math>, so these unordered pairs number <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ℓ</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>𝐿</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> (a hub of degree at least <math><mn>2</mn></math> is one of the <math><mi>𝑥</mi></math> vertices and has at most <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> such neighbors, and a hub of degree <math><mn>1</mn></math> has none), and they contribute at most <math><mi>𝐿</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn></math> to the sum over ordered pairs.</p><p><em>Two vertices of degree at least 2.</em> If non-adjacent with a common neighbor, their covariance is at most <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>18</mn></math> by <a href="#lem-cov-bound">Lemma 2</a> (they are not two leaves at the same hub). The ordered non-adjacent pairs among these <math><mi>𝑥</mi></math> vertices number <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math>, where <math><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> counts the edges between them. A vertex of degree at least <math><mn>2</mn></math> carrying no leaf has at least two such edges and at most <math><mi>𝐿</mi></math> vertices carry a leaf, so <math><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup></math>.</p><p><em>Adjacent pairs</em> have negative covariance, and we keep only the two ordered pairs formed by a leaf and its hub <math><mi>𝑤</mi></math>, which contribute <math><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix">−</mo><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑤</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mo form="prefix">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math> together when <math><mi>𝑤</mi></math> has degree at least <math><mn>2</mn></math>. The two vertices of an isolated edge are each other’s hub, and the edge contributes <math><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mo form="prefix">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math> for its two leaves once <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. In all, the kept pairs contribute at most <math><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐿</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math>.</p><p>Adding up,</p><div class="eq" id="eq-star-profile"><math display="block"><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>𝐿</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑥</mi></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐿</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝐿</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑥</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><mn>18</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>𝐿</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(29)</div></div><p>to be compared with <math><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, the value of the same decomposition on the star (it is <a href="#eq-star">Eq. (7)</a>).</p><p><em>Case <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.</em> Then <math><mi>𝐿</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>≤</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math> since <math><mi>𝐺</mi></math> is not the star, and <a href="#eq-star-profile">Eq. (29)</a> gives <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</p><p><em>Case <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.</em> The right-hand side of <a href="#eq-star-profile">Eq. (29)</a> increases with <math><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></math>, so <math><msup><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></math> may be replaced by <math><mi>𝐿</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑥</mi></math>, after which <math><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> minus the right-hand side equals</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑥</mi></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑥</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><mn>18</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mi>.</mi></math><div class="eq-num">(30)</div></div><p>As a function of a real variable, <math><mi>𝐷</mi></math> is concave on <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> and on <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> (its only non-linear terms are <math><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>18</mn></math> and <math><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup><mi>/</mi><mn>9</mn></math>, and the second is convex, which is why the interval is split), so on each interval it is at least the smaller of its values at the endpoints:</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mtable class="multiline-equation aligned"><mtr><mtd><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow><mn>36</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>36</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><mn>72</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑛</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>36</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></math><div class="eq-num">(31)</div></div><p>At <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math> these are <math><mn>4</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>36</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>49</mn></math>, <math><mn>0.168</mn><mi>…</mi></math> and <math><mn>32</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>36</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>36</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>49</mn></math>, all positive. For <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> increases with <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> from <math><mn>7</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>36</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>64</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>36</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>18</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>72</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>30</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>36</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>72</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>36</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>4</mn></math>. Hence <math><mi>𝐷</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></math> for every integer <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math>, that is <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</p><p><em>Isolated vertices.</em> Let <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and let <math><mi>𝐺</mi></math> have <math><mi>𝑖</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math> isolated vertices. They are peaks of every labeling, so <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> equals the variance on the graph <math><msup><mi>𝐺</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> obtained by deleting them, which has no isolated vertex: either <math><msup><mi>𝐺</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> is empty and <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, or <math><msup><mi>𝐺</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> has <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑖</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math> vertices and <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mi>𝑖</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> by the above. By <a href="#eq-star">Eq. (7)</a>, <math><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, which increases strictly with <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math> (its increments are <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></math>), so <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><msub><mtext>St</mtext><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> in both cases. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></p></div><p>The companion code checks this result on various families of graphs, including all graphs on <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>7</mn></math> vertices.</p></div>

{#sec-app-path-cycle}
## C Path and cycle: proofs and derivations

```{raw} html
<div class="typst"><p><strong>Degree-driven means.</strong> The path and cycle are two cases of a general pattern: by <a href="#thm-mean">Theorem 1</a> the mean depends on the graph through its degrees alone, so it is a simple closed form the moment the degree sequence is known. For a graph on <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> vertices with <math><mi>ℓ</mi></math> leaves and <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ℓ</mi></math> vertices of degree <math><mi>𝑑</mi></math>, the monochrome mean is</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mi>𝑑</mi><mrow><mi>𝑑</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(32)</div></div><p>and for general <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> the two terms become <math><mi>ℓ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝜌</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝜌</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑑</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Taking <math><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> gives the <math><mi>𝑑</mi></math>-regular graphs. The cycle is <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑑</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and the path is <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑑</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, while the <math><mi>𝑑</mi></math>-regular trees have <math><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></math> (though <math><mi>ℓ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></math> does not force a tree). The variance is not degree-driven this way: it depends on the joint degrees of neighboring vertices through <a href="#thm-sfm">Theorem 3</a>, so no comparable closed form holds for it.</p><div><p><em>Proof of <a href="#cor-path-cycle-var">Corollary 4</a>.</em> By <a href="#eq-var-local">Eq. (6)</a> only the pairs at distance one and two contribute. On the cycle with <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></math> every vertex is a peak with probability <math><mi>𝜌</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝜌</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, its two neighbors form with it ordered pairs with parameters <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and its two vertices at distance two pairs with parameters <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, so</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><msub><mi>𝐶</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝜌</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜌</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝜌</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝜌</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(33)</div></div>and evaluating the integrals of <a href="#eq-tsame-tdist">Eq. (4)</a> at these parameters gives the stated coefficient. On the path with <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math> the two endpoints are peaks with probability <math><msub><mi>𝜌</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, the four ordered adjacent pairs they belong to have parameters <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> or <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and the four ordered pairs at distance two <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> or <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The <math><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> other adjacent pairs and <math><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> other pairs at distance two are as on the cycle. The difference with the cycle is the stated boundary term. At <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝜌</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>15</mn></math>, so <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><msub><mi>𝐶</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>15</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>45</mn></math>. The monochrome moments of the path are classical <span id="loc-107">[</span><a href="#loc-83" role="doc-biblioref">Hiv+07</a>, <a href="#loc-104" role="doc-biblioref">WS96</a>]. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><div><p><em>Proof of <a href="#thm-path-cycle-law">Theorem 7</a>.</em> <em>Monochrome path.</em> Removing the smallest value of a permutation of size at least <math><mn>2</mn></math> splits it either at an end (leaving one permutation) or in the interior (leaving two independent ones). The removed element is never a peak, and its neighbors beat it, so their peak status is unchanged once they become endpoints of the pieces, while the permutation of size <math><mn>1</mn></math> is a peak. This gives the Riccati equation <math><msub><mi>𝜕</mi><mi>𝑧</mi></msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑃</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝑃</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> with <math><mi>𝑃</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, whose solution is <a href="#eq-peak-egf">Eq. (11)</a> [<a href="#loc-65" role="doc-biblioref">Ent69</a>, <a href="#loc-106" role="doc-biblioref">Zhu16</a>]. The probability generating function of <math><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> follows by marking non-peaks, <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑢</mi><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑢</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>𝑃</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑢</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Coefficient extraction gives <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>3</mn></math> and, for <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>45</mn></math>, in agreement with <a href="#cor-path-cycle-mean">Corollary 3</a> and <a href="#cor-path-cycle-var">Corollary 4</a>.</p><p><em><math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored path.</em> Under a uniform <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-coloring a vertex is a peak when it exceeds its <em>same-color</em> neighbors only, so the path breaks at every color change into maximal monochromatic runs whose peaks are independent. Each run is a monochrome path, counted by <math><mi>𝑃</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, and consecutive runs carry distinct colors. Summing over the number of runs gives <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑃</mi><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑃</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, whose value at <math><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, i.e. <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup></math>, the number of labeled <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored paths.</p><p><em>Monochrome oriented cycle.</em> The cycle of length <math><mn>1</mn></math> is a loop and its vertex is not a peak, by convention. In an oriented cycle of size at least <math><mn>2</mn></math>, removing the minimum-labeled vertex, which is never a peak, produces an oriented path whose endpoints keep their peak status, hence <math><mi>𝑌</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>𝑧</mi></msubsup><mi>𝑃</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑦</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑦</mi></math>, which integrates to the closed form of <a href="#eq-path-cycle-egf">Eq. (12)</a>. In particular the peak count of <math><msub><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> has the law of that of <math><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math>, which transfers the monochrome moments and the central limit theorem of the path to the cycle. The mean <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>3</mn></math> and variance <math><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>45</mn></math> (for <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></math>) of the series are those of <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> in <a href="#cor-path-cycle-mean">Corollary 3</a> and <a href="#cor-path-cycle-var">Corollary 4</a>.</p><p><em><math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored oriented cycle.</em> Let <math><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> (resp. <math><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>) count <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored paths whose first and last vertices have the same (resp. distinct) colors. Any path is in one of the two cases, and a path with same-color ends is either monochrome, or decomposes uniquely as a path with distinct-color ends followed by a monochrome path of the color of its starting point, so</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑃</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑃</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mspace width="1em"></mspace><mspace width="1em"></mspace><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑃</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(34)</div></div><p>hence</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑃</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑃</mi></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑃</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑃</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mspace width="1em"></mspace><mspace width="1em"></mspace><msub><mi>𝑃</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑃</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑃</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑃</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mi>.</mi></math><div class="eq-num">(35)</div></div><p>A <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored oriented cycle of size <math><mn>1</mn></math> contributes <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>𝑧</mi></math>. Otherwise, removing the vertex of label <math><mn>1</mn></math> leaves a <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored path whose ends keep their peak status, and the removed vertex is a peak in the cycle iff its color differs from the colors of both ends of this path: when the ends share a color, <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> colors make it a peak and one does not, whereas when they differ, <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math> do and two do not. This is <a href="#eq-cycle-kcol-egf">Eq. (13)</a>, which collapses to <math><mi>𝑌</mi></math> at <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. The cycles of length <math><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mn>2</mn></math>, a loop and a double edge, are outside the simple-graph model. Their terms are the normalizations that make the differential equations hold, and the series describe <math><msub><mi>𝐶</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> for <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></p></div><p>The companion code checks all four series.</p></div>
```

{#sec-app-trees}
## D Random trees: proofs and derivations

```{raw} html
<div class="typst"><p>The companion code checks the moments of <a href="#cor-tree-moments">Corollary 6</a>.</p><p><strong>The <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored mean.</strong> By <a href="#thm-mean">Theorem 1</a>, <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝜌</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐷</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> with <math><mi>𝐷</mi></math> the degree of a uniform vertex and <math><msub><mi>𝜌</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑑</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><msubsup><mo form="prefix">∫</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msup><mi>𝑡</mi><mi>𝑑</mi></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑡</mi></math>. The number of labeled trees on <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> vertices in which a given vertex has degree <math><mi>𝑑</mi></math> is <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0"><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑑</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mi>𝑑</mi></mrow></msup></math>, so <math><mi>𝐷</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>∼</mo><mtext>Binomial</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑡</mi><mi>𝐷</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, which is <a href="#eq-tree-kmean">Eq. (17)</a>. Since <math><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mi>𝑡</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> uniformly on <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> and <math><mi>𝑘</mi><msubsup><mo form="prefix">∫</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mi>𝑡</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mi>𝑡</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup></math>, the mean is <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. In closed form, with <math><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math>, the integral of <a href="#eq-tree-kmean">Eq. (17)</a> is</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><msubsup><mo lspace="0em">∫</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mi>𝑡</mi><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑚</mi></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑡</mi><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑏</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><msup><mi>𝑏</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(36)</div></div><p>so that <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math> times this bracket. At <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> the bracket equals <math><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the formula reduces to <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.</p><p><strong>The <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored variance.</strong> By <a href="#cor-triangle-free">Corollary 1</a> only the pairs at distance at most two contribute to the covariance, and in a tree the neighborhood profile of such a pair is read off the degrees of its two vertices: with the parameters <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> of <a href="#sec-general">Section 3</a>, <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, and <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> when <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></math> is an edge or when <math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> are at distance two (then <math><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>), <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> beyond.</p><div class="env env-lemma" id="lem-tree-pairs"><div><strong>Lemma 3 (Pairs of vertices in a Cayley tree).</strong><div class="em"><p>In the uniform random labeled tree on <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math> vertices, for two fixed distinct vertices <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></math> and all real <math><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑡</mi></math>:</p><ol><li><math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑠</mi><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub></msup><msup><mi>𝑡</mi><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mi>𝑡</mi><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>: the vector <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is multinomial with <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math> trials and probabilities <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math>.</li><li><math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> are adjacent with probability <math><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math>, and then <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑠</mi><mi>𝑎</mi></msup><msup><mi>𝑡</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>: <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is the sum of a multinomial vector with <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math> trials and probabilities <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math> and of a vector uniform on <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math>.</li><li><math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> are at distance two with probability <math><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, and then <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑠</mi><mi>𝑎</mi></msup><msup><mi>𝑡</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math>: <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is the sum of a multinomial vector with <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math> trials and probabilities <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></math> and of a vector uniform on <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></math>.</li></ol></div></div></div><div><p><em>Proof.</em> Let <math><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be the Cayley tree function of <a href="#sec-trees">Section 5.2</a>, with <math><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math>, the exponential generating function of rooted labeled trees. A tree with an ordered pair of distinct distinguished vertices <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></math> is the path <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑣</mi></math> (<math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math>) together with a rooted tree hanging from each <math><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></math>. Mark by <math><mi>𝑠</mi></math> (resp. <math><mi>𝑡</mi></math>) the children of the root of the tree hanging from <math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> (resp. <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math>), that is, the <math><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> (resp. <math><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>) neighbors of <math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> (resp. <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math>) off the path. A rooted tree whose root has its children marked by <math><mi>𝑠</mi></math> has generating function <math><mi>𝑧</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mi>𝑠</mi><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math>. Summing over all <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, keeping <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> only, or keeping <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> only gives, for all pairs, adjacent pairs and pairs at distance two,</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><msub><mi>𝐴</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mspace width="1em"></mspace><msub><mi>𝐴</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mspace width="1em"></mspace><msub><mi>𝐴</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(37)</div></div><p>and in the last two cases <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑢</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑑</mi><mi>𝑣</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Since <math><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math>, each <math><msub><mi>𝐴</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is <math><msub><mi>𝐻</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with <math><msub><mi>𝐻</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑢</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑢</mi></mrow></msup></math>, <math><msub><mi>𝐻</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑢</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑢</mi></mrow></msup></math> and <math><msub><mi>𝐻</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑢</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑠</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑢</mi></mrow></msup></math>. The Lagrange inversion formula <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>𝐻</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo expectation over the tree can be taken inside the bracket, where <a href="#lem-tree-pairs">Lemma 3</a> gives <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo For the asymptotics write <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><msub><mi>𝜇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> and <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝜈</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math>. Uniformly for bounded <math><mi>𝑧</mi></math>, <math><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo <math><msub><mi>𝜇</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo
```
