<math><msub><mi>𝜇</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> sharpens <a href="#eq-tree-kmean">Eq. (17)</a> to <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, whose constant is <math><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑒</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> at <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> as in <a href="#eq-tree-moments">Eq. (16)</a>. In the slope, <math><mi>𝜇</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup></math> and <math><mi>𝜇</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math> are the probabilities that a Poisson variable of mean <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math> equals <math><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mn>1</mn></math>, so <math><msubsup><mi>𝜎</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></math>. Numerically <math><msubsup><mi>𝜎</mi><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.147</mn></math> and <math><msubsup><mi>𝜎</mi><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.146</mn></math>, and <math><msubsup><mi>𝜎</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, so that the variance and the mean of <math><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> become equivalent as <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> grows.</p><div><em>Proof of <a href="#thm-clt-tree">Theorem 9</a>.</em> By <a href="#prop-tree-leaves">Proposition 5</a> the peak count <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> has the same law as the number of leaves of a uniform random labeled tree. The number of leaves, and more generally the number of vertices of any fixed degree, of a uniform random labeled tree (equivalently a Galton-Watson tree conditioned on its size) obeys a central limit theorem [<a href="#loc-61" role="doc-biblioref">Drm09</a>]. Its variance is of order <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> by <a href="#cor-tree-moments">Corollary 6</a>, so the limit is nondegenerate. Since <math><msub><mi>𝑇</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> is affine in <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math>, it is asymptotically normal with the stated centering and scaling. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><div class="env env-proposition" id="prop-tree-gw"><div><strong>Proposition 11 (Poisson Galton-Watson tree).</strong><div class="em"><p>For the Galton-Watson tree with <math><mtext>Poisson</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> offspring, the probability generating function of the number of peaks is</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>𝑒</mi></mfrac><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mspace width="1em"></mspace><mtext>valid for</mtext><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>.</mi></math><div class="eq-num">(42)</div></div></div></div></div><div><p><em>Proof.</em> Write <math><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑧</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑧</mi></math> for <a href="#eq-tree-peak-gf">Eq. (14)</a>, so that <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝜏</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><mrow><mtext>peaks</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜏</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math> over the <math><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> rooted labeled trees of size <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math>. A Poisson<math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> Galton-Watson tree has total-progeny law <math><mtext>ℙ</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝒯︀</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑚</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>𝑚</mi><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>!</mo></math> and, conditioned on its size <math><mi>𝑚</mi></math> and given a uniform random vertex labeling, is a uniform rooted labeled tree (a Cayley tree) [<a href="#loc-61" role="doc-biblioref">Drm09</a>]. As a peak depends only on the relative order of labels, its peak probability generating function is therefore</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><munder><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><mtext>ℙ</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>𝒯︀</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>𝑚</mi><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><munder><mo form="prefix">∑</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝜏</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">=</mo><mi>𝑚</mi></mrow></munder><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><mrow><mtext>peaks</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜏</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><munder><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munder><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑚</mi></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑚</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>.</mi></math><div class="eq-num">(43)</div></div>Since <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, this equals <math><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi></math>. Equivalently, it is <a href="#eq-tree-peak-gf">Eq. (14)</a> composed with the Poisson size generating function <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. It converges for <math><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, where the argument has modulus at most <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑒</mi></math>, the radius of convergence of <math><mi>𝐶</mi></math>. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><p>The Poisson<math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> tree is critical, so its size, and with it its peak count, has infinite mean. Conditioning on the size <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> returns the exact law of <a href="#thm-tree-dist">Theorem 8</a> and the finite moments of <a href="#cor-tree-moments">Corollary 6</a>. By <a href="#prop-tree-leaves">Proposition 5</a> this is also the leaf probability generating function of the Poisson<math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> tree.</p><p><strong>General rooted trees.</strong> Consider rooted labeled <em>plane</em> trees (ordered children) carrying a weight <math><msub><mi>𝜑</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msub></math> on each node of out-degree <math><mi>𝑐</mi></math>, with <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑐</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝜑</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msub><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msup></math>, so that the unmarked generating function obeys the classical <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. For the Cayley weights <math><msub><mi>𝜑</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>!</mo></math> this is the uniform unordered labeled tree. To mark peaks we use a catalytic variable <math><mi>𝑥</mi></math> that records the <em>holes</em> of a node (the slots where a further child could be inserted), so a node of out-degree <math><mi>𝑐</mi></math> with <math><mi>𝑑</mi></math> holes weighs <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0"><mrow><mi>𝑐</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑑</mi></mrow><mi>𝑐</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝜑</mi><mrow><mi>𝑐</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mi>𝑑</mi></mrow></msub></math> and a full child-and-hole set has generating function <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</p><div class="env env-proposition" id="thm-gtree"><div><strong>Proposition 12 (General rooted trees and Galton-Watson trees).</strong><div class="em"><p>Let <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be the generating function of weighted rooted labeled trees in which <math><mi>𝑧</mi></math> marks the nodes, <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> the peaks and <math><mi>𝑥</mi></math> the holes. It is characterized by</p><div class="eq" id="eq-gtree-pde"><math display="block"><msub><mi>𝜕</mi><mi>𝑧</mi></msub><mi>𝐴</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐴</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝜕</mi><mi>𝑥</mi></msub><mi>𝐴</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐴</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(44)</div></div><p>and the monochrome peak generating function is <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. For <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mi>𝑧</mi></msup></math> it is <a href="#eq-tree-peak-gf">Eq. (14)</a>. If <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></math> is a probability generating function of mean at most <math><mn>1</mn></math>, other than <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑧</mi></math>, then <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is the peak probability generating function of the Galton-Watson tree with offspring law <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></math>. Under a uniform <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-coloring, the generating function <math><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> of trees whose root has a prescribed color satisfies</p><div class="eq" id="eq-gtree-kcol"><math display="block"><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo></math><div class="eq-num">(45)</div></div>and the generating function of all <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored trees is <math><mi>𝑘</mi><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</div></div></div><p><strong>Proof.</strong> Letting <math><mi>𝑧</mi></math> mark nodes, <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> peaks and <math><mi>𝑥</mi></math> holes, removing the smallest-labeled node gives <a href="#eq-gtree-pde">Eq. (44)</a>: the removed node is either the root (first two terms, according to whether it is a peak, which happens iff it has no children) or an internal node whose removal turns its parent slot into a hole (last term). The quantity of interest is <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. For the Cayley weights <math><msub><mi>𝜑</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑐</mi><mo>!</mo></math>, i.e. <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mi>𝑧</mi></msup></math>, a hole behaves like a marked child slot at a single node and <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mi>𝑥</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with <math><mi>𝐹</mi></math> as in <a href="#eq-tree-peak-gf">Eq. (14)</a>, which satisfies the equation and reduces at <math><mi>𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> to <a href="#eq-tree-peak-gf">Eq. (14)</a>. If <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></math> is a probability generating function of mean at most <math><mn>1</mn></math>, other than <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑧</mi></math> (so that the tree is almost surely finite), then <math><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is well defined for <math><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and is the peak probability generating function of the Galton-Watson tree with offspring law <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></math>. The Poisson<math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> case recovers <a href="#prop-tree-gw">Proposition 11</a>. Unlike the Cayley case, peaks and leaves are not equidistributed in general: for the full binary offspring law the tree on three vertices has peak generating function <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>3</mn></math> and leaf generating function <math><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.</p><p>For the random coloring, consider a <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored general rooted tree with holes and keep only the vertices of some fixed color, say <em>red</em>. The connected component containing the root is a monochrome (red) general rooted tree with holes, in which each hole either was already a hole in the original tree, or held the root of a <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored subtree whose root is one of the <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> non-red colors. Since a hole and such an attached non-red subtree play the same structural role at a red vertex, a child slot that does not affect the red vertex’s peak status, the two combine additively in the holes variable. Writing <math><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> for the generating function of <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-colored general rooted trees with a red root and no hole, this gives <a href="#eq-gtree-kcol">Eq. (45)</a>, and summing over the <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> root colors gives <math><mi>𝑘</mi><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. In the Cayley case <math><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, which Lagrange inversion solves (<a href="#thm-tree-klaw">Theorem 10</a>).</p><div><p><em>Proof of <a href="#thm-tree-klaw">Theorem 10</a>.</em> Orient the edges away from the root (peaks do not depend on it) and condition on the set <math><mi>𝑀</mi></math> of initially conflicting edges. Each non-root vertex has the color of its parent with probability <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>, independently of the others, so <math><mtext>ℙ</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑀</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑀</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>𝑀</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>𝑀</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msup></math> for every <math><msub><mi>𝑀</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>⊆</mo><mi>𝐸</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, and a vertex is a peak iff it is a local maximum of the forest <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑉</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, whose components are monochrome: given <math><mi>𝑀</mi></math> with components <math><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>𝑚</mi></msub></math> of sizes <math><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mi>𝑚</mi></msub></math>, <math><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∏</mo><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><mrow><mtext>peaks</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math>. The rooted trees containing a given spanning forest <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></math> with these components number <math><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>⋯</mi><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mi>𝑚</mi></msub></math>, that is <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> roots times the unrooted count <math><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>⋯</mi><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mi>𝑚</mi></msub></math> [<a href="#loc-93" role="doc-biblioref">Moo70</a>, <a href="#loc-96" role="doc-biblioref">Pit99</a>], which is the weighted Cayley formula <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝜏</mi></msub><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∏</mo><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>𝑖</mi><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">deg</mo><mi>𝜏</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑖</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>⋯</mi><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>𝑚</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>⋯</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>𝑚</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> over the trees <math><mi>𝜏</mi></math> on the <math><mi>𝑚</mi></math> contracted components, at <math><msub><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></math>. Summing over the trees containing <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></math>, then over the spanning forests with <math><mi>𝑚</mi></math> components,</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><munderover><mo form="prefix">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi></munderover><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>𝑘</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><munder><mo form="prefix">∑</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></munder><munderover><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi>𝑖</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>𝑚</mi></munderover><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><mrow><mtext>peaks</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mi>.</mi></math><div class="eq-num">(46)</div></div>The factor <math><msub><mi>𝑐</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></math> roots the component <math><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></math>, and rooted labeled trees by peaks have the exponential generating function <math><mi>𝐹</mi></math>, so the inner sum is <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑚</mi></msup><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>!</mo></math>. Since <math><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math>, the sum over <math><mi>𝑚</mi></math> is <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msub><mo form="prefix">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝐹</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑚</mi></msup><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>𝑚</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, which is <a href="#eq-tree-klaw">Eq. (19)</a>. At <math><mi>𝑣</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mi>𝑎</mi><mi>𝐶</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>!</mo></math> [<a href="#loc-75" role="doc-biblioref">FS09</a>] give <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Alternatively, with <math><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub></mrow></msup></math> the fixed point of <a href="#thm-gtree">Proposition 12</a> reads <math><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></math>, and Lagrange inversion gives <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑢</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. As <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub></math> counts the colored trees whose root has a prescribed color, <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑣</mi><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msub><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, the same formula. Expanded, the right-hand side of <a href="#eq-tree-klaw">Eq. (19)</a> is a polynomial in <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>, whose value at <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>𝐹</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the monochrome law of <a href="#thm-tree-dist">Theorem 8</a>. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><p><strong>A binary-tree observation.</strong> On rooted full binary <em>plane</em> trees with <math><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> labeled vertices, the number of labelings with exactly one peak appears to be <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑚</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo form="postfix">!</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>𝑧</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑚</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">cos</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑧</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the sequence OEIS A395382: we checked the identity for <math><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>10</mn></math> but have not proved it.</p></div>

{#sec-app-er}
## E Erdős-Rényi graphs: proofs and variance

```{raw} html
<div class="typst"><div><em>Proof of <a href="#prop-er-mean">Proposition 6</a>.</em> List the vertices by decreasing label as in <a href="#sec-families">Section 5</a>, so that the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th vertex has the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th largest label. It is a peak with probability <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> with <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mtext>Binomial</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, that is <math><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Summing over <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math> gives <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. This expression depends on <math><mi>𝑝</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> only through <math><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>, so the mean under a uniform <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math>-coloring at edge probability <math><mi>𝑝</mi></math> equals the monochrome mean at edge probability <math><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>. Indeed, a vertex of larger label than the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th prevents it from being a peak iff it shares its color and is adjacent to it, an event of probability <math><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>, as in the monochrome case at <math><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>. This equality fails for the variance, which depends on pairs of vertices. The conflicting edges form <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> separate random graphs, one per color class, not a single <math><mi>𝐺</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>: two vertices of distinct colors never interact. For instance, at <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝑝</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.2</mn></math>, <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> the variance is <math><mn>3.38</mn></math>, against <math><mn>3.60</mn></math> monochrome at <math><mi>𝑝</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></math>. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><p>The same reading gives the second factorial moment in a few stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑖</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑖</mi><mo lspace="0em" href="#prop-er-limit">Proposition 7</a>.</div></div></div><div><em>Proof.</em> Given the colors the peak indicators are independent, so <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mo form="prefix">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">&lt;</mo><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>, the expectation being over the colors. If the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th and <math><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math>-th vertices share their color (probability <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>), each of the <math><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> vertices of larger label than the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th is counted in both <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></math> and <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></math> with probability <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>, whence a factor <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝑡</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> each; each of the <math><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> vertices in between is counted in <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></math> with probability <math><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>, whence a factor <math><mi>𝑠</mi></math>; and the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th vertex itself is counted in <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></math>, whence the factor <math><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi></math>. If their colors differ (probability <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>), a vertex of larger label than the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th is counted once with probability <math><mn>2</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></math>, whence a factor <math><msub><mi>𝑡</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, the vertices in between contribute <math><mi>𝑠</mi></math> each and the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th vertex <math><mn>1</mn></math>. Summing the geometric series over <math><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> gives <a href="#eq-er-sfm">Eq. (47)</a>. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><p><strong>Random graph and fixed graph.</strong> The generating functions <a href="#eq-er-gf">Eq. (20)</a> and <a href="#eq-er-gf-k">Eq. (21)</a> and every random-graph formula of the paper describe the joint law over the graph, the coloring and the labeling. For a fixed graph the peak indicators are dependent, and the joint variance is the mean, over the graph, of the variance on a fixed graph, plus the variance, over the graph, of the mean on a fixed graph. Only the first term measures the fluctuations of the stabilization time on one fixed network. The second measures the differences between networks.</p><p><strong>Palette on random graphs.</strong> On <math><mi>𝐺</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> the maximum degree <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math> is random, so the condition <math><mi>𝑞</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> concerns the palette relative to a random quantity. Taking <math><mi>𝑞</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi></math> always satisfies it. More economically, for <em>constant</em> <math><mi>𝑝</mi></math> one has <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑜</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑝</mi></math> with high probability [<a href="#loc-86" role="doc-biblioref">JŁR00</a>], so any palette <math><mi>𝑞</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝜀</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑝</mi></math> meets <math><mi>𝑞</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> with probability <math><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑜</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. On that event <math><mi>𝑇</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑆</mi></math> holds exactly and the excluded draws contribute a vanishing correction. When <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑝</mi></math> stays bounded, this fails: the mean degree is constant but <math><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">log</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>/</mi><mo form="prefix" lspace="0.16666666666666666em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">log</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">log</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, so the palette must grow at least that fast. The peak statistic <math><mi>𝑆</mi></math>, and hence every mean and variance formula, is defined for any <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> with no palette constraint. The bound <math><mi>𝑞</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is only what ties it to the algorithm’s recoloring count.</p><p><strong>Variance through the second factorial moment theorem.</strong> Unlike the triangle-free families, <math><mi>𝐺</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> has triangles, so its variance exercises the full <a href="#thm-sfm">Theorem 3</a>, and the computation below is the one that the bipartite model reuses (<a href="#sec-app-bip">Appendix F</a>). Averaging over the random graph makes the neighborhood profile of a pair explicit: for a random ordered pair <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑢</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑣</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, each of the other <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math> vertices is independently a common neighbor with probability <math><mi>𝛽</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, a private neighbor of <math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> (resp. <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math>) with probability <math><mi>𝛼</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, or neither with probability <math><mi>𝛿</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, so <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is multinomial. Since <math><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub></math> and <math><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub></math> are expectations of products whose exponents are exactly <math><mi>𝑎</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑏</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑐</mi></math>, this multinomial average collapses the sum of <a href="#eq-sfm">Eq. (5)</a> into closed forms.</p><div class="env env-proposition" id="prop-er-var"><div><strong>Proposition 14 (Erdős-Rényi, variance).</strong><div class="em"><p>On <math><mi>𝐺</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> colors, write <math><mi>𝛼</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, <math><mi>𝛽</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, <math><mi>𝛿</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. The variance of the stabilization time is <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑇</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> with <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> as in <a href="#eq-er-mean">Eq. (22)</a> and</p><div class="eq" id="eq-er-var"><math display="block"><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝐼</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo class="eq-num">(48)</div></div><p>where, with <math><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><msub><mi>𝐼</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub></math> and This is the <em>joint</em> variance over the random graph, the random coloring, and the random labeling.</div></div></div><div><p><em>Proof.</em> Adjacency of <math><mi>𝑢</mi></math> and <math><mi>𝑣</mi></math> is independent of the other vertices, so a pair is adjacent with probability <math><mi>𝑝</mi></math> (contributing <math><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub></math> only, by <a href="#thm-sfm">Theorem 3</a>) and non-adjacent with probability <math><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi></math> (contributing <math><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub></math>), hence <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.2222em"></mspace><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>. Taking the multinomial expectation of <a href="#eq-tsame-tdist-xy">Eq. (26)</a> and using <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>𝜉</mi><mi>𝑎</mi><mi>𝑎</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>𝜉</mi><mi>𝑏</mi><mi>𝑏</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>𝜉</mi><mi>𝑐</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝛼</mi><msub><mi>𝜉</mi><mi>𝑎</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>𝛽</mi><msub><mi>𝜉</mi><mi>𝑏</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>𝛼</mi><msub><mi>𝜉</mi><mi>𝑐</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>𝛿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> leaves an integrand affine in each variable, which <math><msubsup><mo lspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐴</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑡</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑚</mi></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑡</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐴</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝐵</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝐴</mi><mrow><mi>𝑚</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐵</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑚</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, applied once for <math><msub><mi>𝐼</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub></math> and twice for <math><msub><mi>𝐼</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub></math>, evaluates to the closed forms above (the two symmetric <math><msub><mi>𝜋</mi><mtext>same</mtext></msub></math> terms coincide because <math><mi>𝛼</mi></math> multiplies both private counts). In integral form,</p><div class="eq"><math display="block"><mtable class="multiline-equation aligned"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>𝐼</mi><mtext>dist</mtext></msub></mtd><mtd><mo The factorization of <a href="#eq-er-gf">Eq. (20)</a> is the probability generating function of the independent sum <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></math>. For fixed <math><mi>𝑝</mi></math>, <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑖</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑖</mi></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>∞</mi></math>, so by Borel-Cantelli only finitely many <math><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></math> equal <math><mn>1</mn></math> almost surely and <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>∞</mi></msub></math>, whose mean is <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑖</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑝</mi></math>. When <math><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></math> with <math><mi>𝑛</mi><msub><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>∞</mi></math> the summands are bounded and <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑖</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">&lt;</mo><mi>𝑛</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑖</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑖</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> diverges, so Lindeberg’s condition holds and <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> is asymptotically normal. With <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> colors, condition on the color classes: they induce vertex-disjoint subgraphs with independent edge sets, a class of size <math><mi>𝑚</mi></math> carries a peak count distributed as <a href="#eq-er-gf">Eq. (20)</a> with <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math> replaced by <math><mi>𝑚</mi></math>, and all class sizes tend to infinity almost surely (with <math><mi>𝑚</mi><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>∞</mi></math> in the second regime), so the <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> conditionally independent counts converge jointly to <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> independent copies of the monochrome limit. In the second regime the fluctuation of the conditional mean must be compared with the conditional variance, which is <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑜</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> in probability, while, by the Berry-Esseen bound for independent bounded indicators, the conditional law is within Kolmogorov distance <math><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> of the normal law, uniformly over the class sizes. Writing <math><msub><mi>𝑁</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></math> for the class sizes, the conditional mean is <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>𝑁</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑝</mi></math>, so its deviation from <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is <math><mi>𝐷</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix">−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo form="prefix">∑</mo><mi>𝑖</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>𝑁</mi><mi>𝑖</mi></msub></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> and, by Cauchy-Schwarz, <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐷</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0.16666666666666666em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑁</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with <math><mi>𝑁</mi><mo>∼</mo><mtext>Binomial</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Now <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑁</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑝</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>𝑛</mi></mrow></msup></math>, a difference of <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math>-th powers of two numbers at distance <math><msup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, hence at most <math><mi>𝑛</mi><msup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑝</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup><mo>≤</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><msup><mi>𝑝</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mi>𝑘</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup></math> for <math><mi>𝑝</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Therefore <math><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐷</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mo form="prefix" lspace="0.16666666666666666em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">Var</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑝</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><msup><mi>𝑒</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, which tends to <math><mn>0</mn></math> when <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>∞</mi></math>, and the conditionally Gaussian limit is Gaussian. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></div><p>At fixed <math><mi>𝑝</mi></math> the mean degree grows with <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math>, so the expected number of peaks <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>𝑘</mi><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑝</mi></math> stays bounded and the variance tends to a constant rather than growing linearly (visible in <a href="#fig-vars">Figure 2</a>). The closed forms track this limit exactly. The companion code checks these formulas.</p></div>
```

form="prefix">+</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑝</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mi>𝑦</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑘</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>𝑝</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑦</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>𝑘</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑥</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">d</mo><mi>𝑦</mi><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></math><div class="eq-num">(53)</div></div></div></div></div><p>The companion code checks this formula.</p><div><p><em>Proof of <a href="#prop-bip-limit">Proposition 9</a>.</em> <em>Conditional independence.</em> Attribute each edge to its endpoint of smaller label. Ordering the vertices by decreasing label, the <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th vertex is a peak iff none of its edges to the <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></math> opposite-side vertices of larger label that share its color is present. These edge sets are disjoint for distinct <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>, so conditionally on the sequence of sides and colors the peak indicators are independent with the stated probabilities, which gives the stated generating function.</p><p><em>Limit at fixed <math><mi>𝑝</mi></math>, monochrome.</em> Write <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></math> with <math><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></math> the indicator that the vertex of <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>-th largest label is a peak. Given the sides, <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></math> counts the vertices of the opposite side among the <math><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> vertices of larger label. The sequence of sides is a uniform arrangement of <math><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> first-side and <math><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> second-side symbols, so for a first-side vertex <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></math> is hypergeometric (a sample of size <math><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> without replacement from the other <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> vertices, <math><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> of which lie on the second side), with mean <math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, and symmetrically. By Hoeffding’s comparison of sampling without and with replacement for convex functions <span id="loc-108">[</span><a href="#loc-85" role="doc-biblioref">Hoe63</a>], <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for a first-side vertex and <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for a second-side one. Both are bounded by <math><msup><mi>𝜃</mi><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> with <math><mi>𝜃</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo form="prefix" lspace="0.16666666666666666em" rspace="0.16666666666666666em">min</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜆</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></math> for all <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> and all <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math>, since <math><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑛</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>𝜆</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Hence <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">&gt;</mo><mi>𝐽</mi></mrow></msub><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>𝜃</mi><mi>𝐽</mi></msup><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜃</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> uniformly in <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math>: the tail of <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub></math> beyond the top <math><mi>𝐽</mi></math> vertices is negligible in probability, uniformly in <math><mi>𝑛</mi></math>. For fixed <math><mi>𝐽</mi></math> the top <math><mi>𝐽</mi></math> sides converge in law to i.i.d. Bernoulli(<math><mi>𝜆</mi></math>) draws, so <math><msub><mo lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≤</mo><mi>𝐽</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></math> converges in law to its i.i.d. counterpart. Letting <math><mi>𝐽</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>∞</mi></math> gives <math><msub><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>𝑛</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>∞</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mo form="prefix" lspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑗</mi><mi>∞</mi></msubsup></math>, where, given i.i.d. sides with <math><mtext>ℙ</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>first side</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝜆</mi></math>, the <math><msubsup><mi>𝐵</mi><mi>𝑗</mi><mi>∞</mi></msubsup></math> are independent Bernoulli<math><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The limit <math><msubsup><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>∞</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math> is almost surely finite since its mean is. The mean follows: a first-side vertex at position <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math> has <math><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mtext>Binomial</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑗</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, so <math><mtext>𝔼</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>ℎ</mi><mi>𝑗</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>𝑗</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, and summing over <math><mi>𝑗</mi></math> with weight <math><mi>𝜆</mi></math>, plus the symmetric term, gives <math><mi>𝜆</mi><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>/</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑝</mi><mi>𝜆</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</p><p><em><math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> colors.</em> Conditionally on the colors, the color classes induce vertex-disjoint bipartite subgraphs with independent edge sets, each with sides of sizes <math><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mi>𝑛</mi></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> and <math><msub><mi>𝑛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>/</mi><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>𝑂</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mi>𝑛</mi></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> in probability, hence with the same side proportion <math><mi>𝜆</mi></math> in the limit. The <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> conditionally independent peak counts converge jointly to <math><mi>𝑘</mi></math> independent copies of <math><msubsup><mi>𝑆</mi><mi>∞</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></math>. <math><mi>∎</mi></math></p></div></div>

{#sec-app-numerics}
## G Numerical checks

```{raw} html
<div class="typst"><p>Two independent programs were used. The first runs the actual recoloring dynamics under the random central daemon (an event loop that draws a uniformly random enabled process at each step and recolors it with a random free color) and records the number of moves. It does not use <a href="#lem-reduction">Lemma 1</a> and serves to check it. The second is a <em>peak-oracle</em> sampler: by <a href="#lem-reduction">Lemma 1</a> one sample of the stabilization time needs only a coloring and a labeling, not a run of the dynamics, which makes large campaigns cheap. On fourteen test graphs (at most seven vertices, listed with the companion code), the law of the move count under the first agrees with the exact law of <math><mi>𝑛</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝑆</mi></math>, computed by enumeration, for <math><mi>𝑘</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></math> initial colors.
```
